title: Pivot Weekdays into Columns
learning_objective: Learn how to create one output row per category with weekday columns.

tutorial.explanation: A pivot-style SQL result uses GROUP BY for rows and conditional aggregation for columns.
tutorial.syntax: SELECT category, SUM(CASE WHEN dow = 1 THEN quantity ELSE 0 END) AS Monday FROM ... GROUP BY category;
tutorial.mental_model: GROUP BY chooses the row grain. Each SUM(CASE WHEN ...) creates one output column.

guided_example.prompt: Return Monday and Tuesday units by category.
guided_example.solution_query: SELECT i.item_category, SUM(CASE WHEN EXTRACT(DOW FROM CAST(o.order_date AS DATE)) = 1 THEN o.quantity ELSE 0 END) AS Monday, SUM(CASE WHEN EXTRACT(DOW FROM CAST(o.order_date AS DATE)) = 2 THEN o.quantity ELSE 0 END) AS Tuesday FROM orders o INNER JOIN items i ON o.item_id = i.item_id GROUP BY i.item_category;
guided_example.explanation: The join adds categories, GROUP BY creates one row per category, and each CASE expression builds a day column.

practice.prompt: Return item_category and Monday units by category.
practice.expected_query: SELECT i.item_category, SUM(CASE WHEN EXTRACT(DOW FROM CAST(o.order_date AS DATE)) = 1 THEN o.quantity ELSE 0 END) AS Monday FROM orders o INNER JOIN items i ON o.item_id = i.item_id GROUP BY i.item_category;

hints: Use SUM(CASE WHEN DOW = 1 THEN quantity ELSE 0 END).
